pathway.title: Aecom — Full credit assessment
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: The business profile is adequate to good for creditors, because scale, a government-funded client base and a large order book give revenue visibility that the third-quarter loss does not undermine. Governments supply 50% of revenue, no client reaches 10%, backlog was $39.7bn at 2025-09-30 and remaining performance obligations were $20.4bn at 2026-06-30, about 60% of them due within twelve months. The work is fee-based and asset-light, so a downturn in one market is cushioned by the others. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-09-30_acm_acm-20250930.htm.jsonl, pages 10–13; 10-Q_2026-07-03_acm_acm-20260703.htm.jsonl, page 15; calculation B18

The financial profile has deteriorated in fiscal 2026 because earnings fell, not because Aecom borrowed more. Calculated EBITDA for the last twelve months is 29.63% below FY2025 while gross debt is almost unchanged, so total leverage rose to 3.21x from 2.26x, interest cover on accrued interest fell to 4.18x from 6.52x, and free cash flow fell to 0.24x of EBITDA from 0.57x. Cash interest cover for the latest period is not established because the quarterly reports print no cash interest. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation B01; calculation B03; calculation B04

Two Construction Management projects are the single most important credit variable. One project took a loss of USD 336.8 million in the third quarter, management expects net cash outflows of USD 600 million to USD 800 million to finish two projects before any claim inflows, claims of about $620 million sit in contract assets, and Aecom has given the clients USD 403.9 million of letters of credit and USD 1.0 billion of surety bonds. Guaranteed-maximum-price and fixed-price work is 61.61% of revenue, so cost overruns land on Aecom, and the projects now account for more than the whole 12-day rise in days sales outstanding to 86 days. Basis: 10-Q_2026-07-03_acm_acm-20260703.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-Q_2026-07-03_acm_acm-20260703.htm.jsonl, pages 35–36; 10-Q_2026-07-03_acm_acm-20260703.htm.jsonl, page 55; 10-Q_2026-07-03_acm_acm-20260703.htm.jsonl, page 56; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation B12; calculation B13; calculation B15

Shareholder returns turned a manageable project outflow into a leverage problem, but the lever is in management's hands. Repurchases plus dividends were 3.29x operating cash flow in the nine months to 2026-06-30 and 8.04x free cash flow, against 0.38x operating cash flow a year earlier. Management says delayed claims could constrain repurchases, none were made from April to June 2026, and USD 884 million of authorization remains, so creditors depend on the pause lasting until the claims are collected. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-07-03_acm_acm-20260703.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-Q_2026-07-03_acm_acm-20260703.htm.jsonl, page 40; 10-Q_2026-07-03_acm_acm-20260703.htm.jsonl, page 41; 10-Q_2026-07-03_acm_acm-20260703.htm.jsonl, page 67; calculation B09; calculation B18

Liquidity and the maturity profile are the main support against the downside. Cash excluding joint-venture cash plus undrawn revolvers covers the full expected outflow 3.45x to 4.60x, only 4.29% of principal falls due through fiscal 2030, the bank facilities now mature in 2031 or 2028 for the new USD 500 million revolver, and the 2033 senior notes were valued at 100.13% of principal at 2026-06-30. Management states that liquidity is sufficient for at least the next twelve months. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-07-03_acm_acm-20260703.htm.jsonl, pages 19–22; 10-Q_2026-07-03_acm_acm-20260703.htm.jsonl, page 54; calculation B05; calculation B10; calculation B16

Structure and covenants are where the credit cannot be fully tested. A consolidated leverage ratio of at most 4.00x is tested quarterly, but its definition and the reported ratio are not printed, so headroom is not established; the bank lenders hold liens on substantially all assets while the 2033 notes are unsecured; and the parent and guarantor group lost USD 168.5 million in nine months and holds 55.66% of consolidated revenue. Goodwill is 1.72x stockholders' equity, so book equity is a thin cushion. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-07-03_acm_acm-20260703.htm.jsonl, pages 21–23; 10-Q_2026-07-03_acm_acm-20260703.htm.jsonl, pages 63–64; calculation B14; calculation B17

The primary downside path is slow or partial claim recovery while outflows run to the top of the range. On reported EBITDA, paying USD 600 million to USD 800 million lifts net leverage to 3.02x to 3.25x before any claim inflow, an illustrative figure that holds everything else constant, against 2.16x to 2.33x if EBITDA were measured before the third-quarter loss. Which of the two is closer depends on whether the project loss is a one-off, which the filings do not settle. Basis: 10-Q_2026-07-03_acm_acm-20260703.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-Q_2026-07-03_acm_acm-20260703.htm.jsonl, page 55; calculation B06; calculation B07

runs.text: Scale and a diversified public-sector client base are the first credit strength. Governments supply 50% of revenue, no client reaches 10%, and backlog of $39.7bn at 2025-09-30 gives revenue visibility, so the business can absorb a problem in one project or market without losing its cash-generating base, which lowers the chance that a single event threatens debt service. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-09-30_acm_acm-20250930.htm.jsonl, pages 10–13; calculation B18

Liquidity and the maturity profile are the second strength. Cash excluding joint-venture cash plus undrawn revolvers covers the full expected project outflow 3.45x to 4.60x and only 4.29% of principal falls due through fiscal 2030, so the project cash cost can be paid without a refinancing, and the bank maturity extension to 2031 removes the nearest pressure point. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-07-03_acm_acm-20260703.htm.jsonl, pages 19–22; calculation B05; calculation B10

A flexible financial policy with no sponsor is the third strength. No sponsor extracts cash, repurchases were paused from April to June 2026, and management has tied their timing to claim collection, so net leverage can rebuild if the pause lasts, although the stated link is not a commitment. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-07-03_acm_acm-20260703.htm.jsonl, page 41; 10-Q_2026-07-03_acm_acm-20260703.htm.jsonl, page 67

Price risk on construction work is the first weakness. Guaranteed-maximum-price and fixed-price contracts are 61.61% of revenue, and on two Construction Management projects delays raised the cost to complete, producing a loss of USD 336.8 million and expected net cash outflows of USD 600 million to USD 800 million, which lifts net debt by the amount paid and exposes Aecom to further estimate changes and to client claims. Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_acm_acm-20250930.htm.jsonl, pages 11–12; 10-Q_2026-07-03_acm_acm-20260703.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-Q_2026-07-03_acm_acm-20260703.htm.jsonl, page 55; calculation B12

Weak cash conversion is the second weakness. Free cash flow was 0.24x of EBITDA over the last twelve months against 0.57x in FY2025 because claims and receivables absorbed cash, and days sales outstanding rose to 86 days, so less cash is available to cut debt or to cover interest even before the project outflows. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-07-03_acm_acm-20260703.htm.jsonl, page 56; calculation B04; calculation B13

Returns that exceeded operating cash flow are the third weakness. Repurchases plus dividends were 3.29x operating cash flow in nine months, so cash fell while debt did not, and the cushion built in FY2025 was spent on shareholders instead of on leverage. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation B09

Untested structure and covenants are the fourth weakness. The covenant ratio is not printed, the parent and guarantor group lost USD 168.5 million in nine months, and goodwill is 1.72x stockholders' equity, so creditors cannot confirm headroom or rely on book equity if earnings fall further. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-07-03_acm_acm-20260703.htm.jsonl, page 21; 10-Q_2026-07-03_acm_acm-20260703.htm.jsonl, pages 63–64; calculation B14; calculation B17

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: On 2026-03-10 Aecom replaced its revolver and term loans with a $1.5bn revolving credit facility and a $950 million term loan A, both maturing on 2031-03-10, and a $500 million term loan B maturing on 2031-04-19. Both term loans were borrowed in full and the proceeds repaid the previous facilities, which had a revolver and term loan A maturing in 2029 and a term loan B maturing in 2031. Bank debt outstanding was USD 1,448.8 million at 2026-06-30 against USD 1,439.9 million at 2025-09-30, so the amendment extended maturities without adding material debt. Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_acm_acm-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 62; 10-Q_2026-07-03_acm_acm-20260703.htm.jsonl, pages 19–20; calculation A17

On 2026-06-10 a separate $500 million revolving facility maturing on 2028-06-09 was added under a new agreement, and it was undrawn with no letters of credit at 2026-06-30. Both bank agreements are secured by liens on substantially all assets of the company and the guarantors, and a consolidated leverage ratio of at most 4.00x is tested quarterly; the covenant does not apply to the term loan B and the company reported compliance at 2026-06-30. Basis: 10-Q_2026-07-03_acm_acm-20260703.htm.jsonl, pages 20–22

On 2025-07-22 Aecom issued $1.2bn of unsecured senior notes due 2033 and used the proceeds to retire the 2027 senior notes: most were bought in a July 2025 tender offer and the remainder was redeemed in August 2025, with make-whole payments of $9.1 million in total. The notes' estimated fair value at 2026-06-30 was $1,201.5 million, close to principal. Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_acm_acm-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 80; 10-Q_2026-07-03_acm_acm-20260703.htm.jsonl, page 22; calculation A16

Acquisitions and disposals have been small or already completed. Two businesses were bought in fiscal 2025 for $375.9 million, including $146.4 million of Aecom shares; the Management Services and self-perform construction businesses were exited earlier and remain in discontinued operations; and the AECOM Capital team moved to a third-party platform in fiscal 2024. The strategic review of the Construction Management business, which the 2025 annual report said could include a sale, was later reported complete with a decision to keep and operate it. Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_acm_acm-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-K_2025-09-30_acm_acm-20250930.htm.jsonl, pages 7–8; 10-K_2025-09-30_acm_acm-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 90; 10-Q_2026-01-02_acm_acm-20260102.htm.jsonl, page 37; 10-Q_2026-04-03_acm_acm-20260403.htm.jsonl, page 40; 10-Q_2026-07-03_acm_acm-20260703.htm.jsonl, pages 9–10; calculation A12

Shareholder returns are the main use of cash apart from debt service. The Board raised the repurchase authorization to $1.0bn on 2024-11-15 and approved an increase to $1.0bn again on 2026-02-04, with $884 million remaining at 2026-06-30, and the quarterly dividend was raised to USD 0.31 per share on 2025-11-18. Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_acm_acm-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 44; 10-K_2025-09-30_acm_acm-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 120; 10-Q_2026-01-02_acm_acm-20260102.htm.jsonl, page 37; 10-Q_2026-07-03_acm_acm-20260703.htm.jsonl, page 40; 10-Q_2026-07-03_acm_acm-20260703.htm.jsonl, page 67

Three events dated after 2026-06-30 are outside the period figures: a quarterly dividend of USD 0.31 per share was paid on 2026-07-17, a settlement of the legacy Department of Energy claims will bring $58.5 million to Aecom with the receipt date not stated, and in August 2026 the tax authority sent a draft notice proposing adjustments to research credits claimed for fiscal 2017 through fiscal 2020, which Aecom disputes and could be material if sustained in full. No new debt or acquisition after 2026-06-30 is stated in the filings. Basis: 10-Q_2026-07-03_acm_acm-20260703.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-07-03_acm_acm-20260703.htm.jsonl, page 29; 10-Q_2026-07-03_acm_acm-20260703.htm.jsonl, page 32

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Source readiness for Aecom (acm-868857), as of 2026-11-18, on the credit snapshot pathway. The scope is whether the five supplied filings can support Financial foundation, Business & governance and Fundamental credit, and what remains blocked.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The five supplied filings support a credit snapshot of Aecom through the third quarter of fiscal 2026, but not covenant headroom, ratings, market pricing or any event after that quarter, so creditor conclusions must stay provisional until those are added.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Financial foundation can run in full, because the statements, debt note and liquidity discussion are present for the latest quarter and two annual periods. Business & governance and Fundamental credit can run with stated limits: no proxy statement, no executed credit documents, no printed covenant ratio, and no result later than the filing signed 2026-08-11, which is 99 days before the as-of date.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The file set is two annual reports (fiscal 2024 and fiscal 2025) and three quarterly reports (the first to third quarters of fiscal 2026), all primary filings by the registrant. Aecom issues the senior notes itself and reports consolidated statements; the subsidiaries that guarantee the notes appear only in summarised combined information, not in separate statements.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The filings use a 52 or 53 week calendar and present every period as if it ended on a calendar quarter end, so the cover of the third-quarter report names a period ending 2026-07-03 while its statements are dated 2026-06-30. Each figure in later work should carry the statement date, with the true period end noted once.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The bank debt terms changed twice in fiscal 2026: an amendment in March 2026 replaced the revolver and both term loans, and a new agreement in June 2026 added a second revolving facility. The annual reports and the first-quarter report therefore describe facilities that have been superseded, and the third-quarter report controls for current terms.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The filings state the maintenance test, a consolidated leverage ratio capped at 4.00x and tested quarterly (the term loan B is exempt), and they say the company complied with its credit agreement covenants at each period end. None prints the ratio, its EBITDA definition or any headroom, and no file uses the term EBITDA, so covenant headroom is not calculable from this file set.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: No file mentions a credit rating or a rating agency, and the run settings supply no quotes, peers or portfolio. Ratings & triggers and Market-implied risk therefore cannot be run from this file set, and relative value lies outside the requested scope.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Business description, risk factors, segments and remaining performance obligations are well covered. The annual reports incorporate director, compensation and ownership information by reference to a proxy statement that is not in the file set, so governance can be described only from what the annual reports themselves print. The latest annual report gives both backlog and remaining performance obligations and states that they differ by USD 20.0 billion; the quarterly reports give only the obligations.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The third-quarter report carries two items that bear directly on later credit work: a loss of USD 336.8 million on one Construction Management project, and management's expectation of net cash outflows of USD 600 million to USD 800 million to complete two such projects, of which USD 175 million to USD 225 million falls in the fourth quarter. The filing quantifies these items but gives no later update.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The latest filing was signed 99 days before the as-of date, and the as-of date falls 49 days after the fiscal 2026 year-end as presented, the same lag at which the fiscal 2025 annual report was signed. The fiscal 2026 annual report may therefore be close but is not in the file set, and nothing in the file set reports the fourth quarter.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C3; 10-Q_2026-07-03_acm_acm-20260703.htm.jsonl, page 7

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The best case that the file set is stronger than it looks is that the primary filings state the covenant level, the facility terms and the project exposures in detail, so Financial foundation and Fundamental credit can proceed without the missing documents. The view would improve if the fiscal 2026 annual report, the executed credit agreement or a compliance certificate were supplied, and would weaken if a later filing revised the third-quarter figures or the project loss estimate, which the third-quarter report itself says may change.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The assessment rests on the five filings and the run settings only; no outside source was consulted, and no judgement on credit quality is made here.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The quarterly statements are unaudited and omit footnotes that the annual reports carry.

fields.value: Financial foundation for Aecom (acm-868857), as of 2026-11-18, on the credit snapshot pathway. The scope is the consolidated statements for FY2024, FY2025 and the nine months to 2026-06-30 as presented, carrying-value debt and net debt, liquidity, calculated EBITDA and the events dated after the latest balance sheet.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Leverage has risen in fiscal 2026 because earnings fell, not because Aecom borrowed more: net debt reached 2.31x last-twelve-months EBITDA at 2026-06-30 against 1.11x at fiscal 2025 year-end, so creditors now carry a thinner cushion ahead of large expected project cash outflows.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Gross leverage was 3.21x against 2.26x because the third quarter absorbed a USD 336.8 million loss on one Construction Management project while debt stayed flat and cash fell. Cash interest cover cannot be measured on the same basis for the latest twelve months because the quarterly report prints no cash interest. Two dated events after quarter-end, a dividend paid on 2026-07-17 and a settlement due in July 2026, take net leverage to 2.36x or 2.24x if each is taken alone.

fields.value: Cash excludes joint-venture cash, and the undrawn figures are revolver availability net of letters of credit, with the newer 500 revolver counted only at 2026-06-30.

fields.value: The ladder is principal at 2026-06-30 and is not split by facility beyond fiscal 2030.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The EBITDA column is reported calculated EBITDA, not an adjusted measure, and the last row is a constructed twelve-month period.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The stack omits other debt and the undrawn revolvers and is not a recovery waterfall.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Leverage is the main concern in the financial foundation, and the cause is earnings rather than borrowing. Gross debt was almost unchanged between 2025-09-30 and 2026-06-30 while calculated EBITDA for the last twelve months fell as the third quarter absorbed a loss of USD 336.8 million on a Construction Management project and nine months of restructuring and acquisition costs, so gross leverage moved from 2.26x to 3.21x and net leverage from 1.11x to 2.31x as cash fell. For creditors the cushion built in fiscal 2025 is being spent on shareholder returns and project cash outflows, not on debt reduction.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_acm_acm-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 77; 10-Q_2026-07-03_acm_acm-20260703.htm.jsonl, pages 2–3; 10-Q_2026-07-03_acm_acm-20260703.htm.jsonl, page 16; calculation C03; calculation C05

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest offsetting evidence is that fiscal year leverage was low and falling before this year: gross leverage fell from 2.50x to 2.26x between FY2024 and FY2025, and cash interest cover on interest actually paid rose from 5.67x to 7.21x. Cover for the latest twelve months cannot be stated on cash paid because the quarterly report omits it; on accrued interest expense it fell from 6.52x to 4.18x, which gives the direction but is not a cash measure. Recovery of the project claims would turn contract assets into cash and ease net debt, whereas further delay would leave a heavier interest burden carried on a smaller earnings base.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash generation weakened sharply in the nine months to 2026-06-30. Operating cash flow of 169.234 (US$m) compares with 625.472 a year earlier, with the filing attributing a 283.5 million increase in outflow to two Construction Management projects, while payments to repurchase shares of 441.862 and dividends of 115.469 (US$m) together exceeded it. Free cash flow after capital expenditure was 203.449 for the last twelve months against 684.927 in FY2025 (US$m), a conversion of 0.24x of EBITDA against 0.57x. Receivables and contract assets absorbed cash, days sales outstanding rose from 74 to 86 and claims inside contract assets rose, so recovery of the claims is the observable test of whether working capital reverses.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-07-03_acm_acm-20260703.htm.jsonl, pages 5–6; 10-Q_2026-07-03_acm_acm-20260703.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-Q_2026-07-03_acm_acm-20260703.htm.jsonl, pages 55–56; calculation C08

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity is adequate against scheduled maturities but is being drawn down, and none of the dated bank facilities expires within the next twelve months. Cash excluding joint-venture cash of 762.018 (US$m) plus undrawn revolvers of 1995.6 gives 2757.618, set against scheduled debt maturities of only 117.8 in total through fiscal 2030 (36.3 in the rest of fiscal 2026 and 34.4 in fiscal 2027), because the March 2026 amendment moved the large bank maturities to 2031, with the 2033 senior notes after them. Against that, management expects net cash outflows of between USD 600 million and USD 800 million to finish two projects, of which USD 175 million to USD 225 million falls in the fourth quarter, before any inflow from claims. Those outflows are not in net debt and would raise it by the amount paid; the filing's maintenance test of 4.00x leverage is not computed here because its definition is not printed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Customer billings and receivable sales are non-debt funding that carries risk of its own. Contract liabilities were 1,129.26 million at 2026-06-30 and trade receivables sold stood at 348.9 million against 268.2 million at 2025-09-30, so reported net debt does not capture all of the funding that supports operations. If a client dispute or a slowdown in advance billings removed either source, the gap would fall on revolver drawings, which is why days sales outstanding and the sold-receivable balance should be watched with debt.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Two dated events after 2026-06-30 are kept out of the period figures. The quarterly dividend paid on 2026-07-17 would lift net leverage to 2.36x and the Department of Energy settlement, if received in full, would lower it to 2.24x, each taken alone against the same EBITDA; the settlement date is stated only as July 2026. The 2026-03-10 refinancing is a multi-figure event: the cash flow statement shows gross borrowings and repayments of about 5.7 billion because the revolver is drawn and repaid regularly and the old term loans were replaced, so gross flows overstate new debt, and the debt note is the source for outstanding amounts.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-07-03_acm_acm-20260703.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-07-03_acm_acm-20260703.htm.jsonl, page 32; 10-Q_2026-07-03_acm_acm-20260703.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-Q_2026-07-03_acm_acm-20260703.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-Q_2026-07-03_acm_acm-20260703.htm.jsonl, page 56; calculation C07

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The main data-quality risks are definitional. EBITDA is calculated because the issuer states none, depreciation and amortization includes amortization of acquired digital assets recorded in cost of revenue, joint-venture cash is excluded from cash, and the FY2024 balance sheet is taken from the later reprint. None changes debt or cash, but together they mean every ratio here is a house measure and should not be compared with a covenant ratio. The most material gaps are the missing covenant ratio and covenant EBITDA, the absence of cash interest for the interim periods and the lack of any figure after the third quarter.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Every ratio here uses EBITDA built from income from operations and depreciation and amortization, and the latest figure is a twelve-month construction from three documents, so none of them is an issuer or covenant measure.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash for net debt leaves out the cash held in consolidated joint ventures, which the filing restricts to those ventures; counting it would lower net debt and flatter every net ratio.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Every derived figure is worked from the printed statement lines; money figures are US$m and ratios are printed to two decimals.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Cash interest paid is not printed for the nine-month periods, so EBITDA over cash interest cannot be calculated for the last twelve months to 2026-06-30 or compared with FY2025. Severity: Medium. Action: add the fiscal 2026 annual report or an earnings release that states interest paid.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The issuer states no EBITDA and no adjusted EBITDA, so EBITDA is calculated from income from operations and depreciation and amortization, the adjusted EBITDA bridge is not stated and covenant EBITDA is unknown. Severity: High for covenant use, Medium otherwise. Action: obtain the covenant definition and a compliance certificate.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Source dashes in the statements are read as missing values, not zero, for restructuring and acquisition costs in the nine months to 2025-06-30, noncontrolling interests from discontinued operations in the nine months to 2026-06-30 and several cash flow lines; the printed subtotals imply no amount. Severity: Low. Action: none needed unless a later filing prints a figure.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Several cash flow lines exist only in the annual statements, for example deferred income tax and impairment, and several only in the quarterly statements, for example non-cash fair value changes, so those columns state the line as not printed. Severity: Low. Action: none; the printed subtotals reconcile.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The first-quarter, second-quarter and discrete third-quarter statements of fiscal 2026 are not extracted into columns; the nine-month statements carry the same flows cumulatively and the last twelve months are built from them, but the path of net debt through 2025-12-31 and 2026-03-31 is not shown. Severity: Low. Action: extract those quarters if a quarter-by-quarter leverage path is wanted.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No balance sheet at 2025-06-30 is printed, so there is no balance sheet column for the nine months to 2025-06-30 and no prior-year interim net debt. Severity: Low. Action: none for the requested use.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The fourth quarter of fiscal 2025 is not printed separately and is not constructed, because the last twelve months to 2026-06-30 needs only the full year and two nine-month stubs. Severity: Low. Action: none.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The debt note prints one balance for the two term loans together and no amortization schedule or drawn balance by facility, so the term loans are one row, the revolvers carry commitments only and the maturity ladder is not split by facility beyond fiscal 2030. Severity: Medium. Action: obtain facility-level balances from the credit agreements.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The legal rank among the credit agreement facilities, and the security and rank of other debt of 96.4 (USD millions), are not stated, so the debt stack shows only the term loans and the 2033 senior notes and omits other debt. Severity: Medium. Action: obtain the credit agreement and the schedule of other debt.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The consolidated perimeter includes joint ventures whose cash is restricted and a guarantor group shown only in summarised combined form, so no restricted-group or guarantor-only leverage can be stated. Severity: Medium. Action: obtain the covenant perimeter definitions.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The fiscal 2025 annual report reprints the FY2024 balance sheet with 120,300 (USD thousands) moved from current to non-current assets; the later reprint is used and no ratio is affected. Severity: Low. Action: none.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Earnings per share and share counts are left out of the statement tables because the tables are in USD thousands. Severity: Low. Action: none for credit use.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No subsequent-events note exists in any quarterly report, so events after 2026-06-30 are limited to the dividend payment and the settlement that the third-quarter report dates; management's expected net cash outflows of USD 600 million to USD 800 million on two projects are an expectation and are not in net debt. Severity: Medium. Action: add the fiscal 2026 annual report and the fourth-quarter release.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Pension and operating lease obligations are outside Total Debt and shown only in the definition register; the pension liability on the balance sheet differs from the aggregate plan deficit the filing states. Severity: Low. Action: a later module may add them knowingly.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Business and governance review of Aecom (acm-868857), as of 2026-11-18, on the credit snapshot pathway. The scope is the business model, ownership and control, transactions, capital allocation and contingent exposures stated in five filings through the quarter ended 2026-06-30.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Aecom is a widely held infrastructure consultancy with no sponsor or controlling holder disclosed, so creditors rely on management's financial policy, and the main weakness is two delayed Construction Management projects that are absorbing earnings and cash.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The wider business is diversified: governments supply 50% of revenue, no client reaches 10%, and International earnings before taxes and amortization reached a 10.35% margin in the nine months to 2026-06-30. Against that, one project took a loss of USD 336.8 million, management expects net cash outflows of USD 600 million to USD 800 million to finish two projects, and in those nine months repurchases plus dividends were 3.29x operating cash flow. Management says delayed claims could constrain repurchases, none were made from April to June 2026, and governance risk is medium.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_acm_acm-20250930.htm.jsonl, pages 10–11; 10-Q_2026-07-03_acm_acm-20260703.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-Q_2026-07-03_acm_acm-20260703.htm.jsonl, page 37; 10-Q_2026-07-03_acm_acm-20260703.htm.jsonl, page 41; 10-Q_2026-07-03_acm_acm-20260703.htm.jsonl, page 55; 10-Q_2026-07-03_acm_acm-20260703.htm.jsonl, page 67; calculation A03; calculation A04

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: No sponsor stands behind the credit, so support in a downturn has to come from the company's own cash flow and bank lines. Aecom is listed on the New York Stock Exchange with widely held shares, the Chairman is also the Chief Executive Officer, and holder percentages are not established because the proxy statement is not supplied. Shares held by non-affiliates were worth about $12.2bn on 2025-03-28.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The core consulting business is diversified and mostly public-sector funded, which is the main support for creditors. Governments supply 50% of revenue and private clients 50%, no client reached 10% of revenue in the past five years, and backlog was $39.7bn at 2025-09-30, $2.3bn higher than a year earlier. Backlog is a gross figure that includes pass-through costs and is $20.0bn above the remaining performance obligations, so it measures visibility, not profit.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Contract terms, not demand, are where the losses come from. Guaranteed-maximum-price and fixed-price work was 61.61% of fiscal 2025 revenue and on both types cost overruns and delay costs can fall on Aecom, while about half of revenue (53% in fiscal 2025) is pass-through subcontractor cost, so one project can erase the margin earned on a large amount of other work. In the quarter to 2026-06-30 the Americas segment reported a gross loss of USD 143.1 million against a gross profit of USD 238.8 million a year earlier.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_acm_acm-20250930.htm.jsonl, pages 11–12; 10-K_2025-09-30_acm_acm-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 53; 10-Q_2026-07-03_acm_acm-20260703.htm.jsonl, pages 48–50; calculation A01

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Two Construction Management projects decide credit quality over the next year, and the business was kept, not sold. Claims for recovery recorded in contract assets rose from about $180 million at 2024-09-30 to about $400 million at 2025-09-30, peaked at about $680 million at 2026-03-31 and stood at about $620 million at 2026-06-30, one project took a loss of USD 336.8 million, and management expects net cash outflows of USD 600 million to USD 800 million to finish two projects, USD 175 million to USD 225 million of it in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026, before any claim inflows. Aecom has also given the project clients corporate guarantees, USD 403.9 million of letters of credit and USD 1.0 billion of surety bonds, and says clients may file a material claim. The strategic review of the business ended with a decision to keep it, so no sale will transfer the exposure.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_acm_acm-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 95; 10-Q_2026-04-03_acm_acm-20260403.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-Q_2026-07-03_acm_acm-20260703.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-Q_2026-07-03_acm_acm-20260703.htm.jsonl, pages 35–36; 10-Q_2026-07-03_acm_acm-20260703.htm.jsonl, page 41; 10-Q_2026-07-03_acm_acm-20260703.htm.jsonl, page 55; 10-Q_2026-04-03_acm_acm-20260403.htm.jsonl, page 40; calculation A06; calculation A07

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Capital allocation has favoured shareholders, but management has named repurchases as the first lever. In the nine months to 2026-06-30 repurchases plus dividends were 3.29x operating cash flow against 0.38x a year earlier, the quarterly dividend rose to USD 0.31 per share from USD 0.26 and USD 0.22, and the USD 1.0 billion authorization had USD 884 million left. Management says further delay in collecting claims could constrain the timing of repurchases, repurchases are discretionary, and no shares were bought from April to June 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2024-09-30_acm_acm-20240930x10k.htm.jsonl, page 121; 10-K_2025-09-30_acm_acm-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 120; 10-Q_2026-07-03_acm_acm-20260703.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-Q_2026-07-03_acm_acm-20260703.htm.jsonl, page 40; 10-Q_2026-07-03_acm_acm-20260703.htm.jsonl, page 41; 10-Q_2026-07-03_acm_acm-20260703.htm.jsonl, page 67; calculation A04; calculation A10

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The guarantor group is weaker than the consolidated company, so the structure matters more than the consolidated figures suggest. The subsidiary guarantors are wholly owned and guarantee the 2033 senior notes, and the bank facilities are secured by liens on substantially all assets of the company and the guarantors. In the nine months to 2026-06-30 the parent and guarantors recorded revenue equal to 55.66% of the consolidated total, a net loss of USD 168.5 million against consolidated net income attributable to Aecom of USD 167.7 million, and a fall in combined equity of USD 237.9 million to USD 362.0 million. Cash held in consolidated joint ventures is restricted to those ventures.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-07-03_acm_acm-20260703.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-07-03_acm_acm-20260703.htm.jsonl, pages 17–18; 10-Q_2026-07-03_acm_acm-20260703.htm.jsonl, pages 21–23; 10-Q_2026-07-03_acm_acm-20260703.htm.jsonl, page 42; 10-Q_2026-07-03_acm_acm-20260703.htm.jsonl, pages 63–64; calculation A08

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Disclosure on structure is good, but the claims disclosure trailed the cash exposure. The auditor has named contract cost and claim recovery estimates a critical audit matter in both annual reports, claims grew each quarter before a loss was recorded, and the second-quarter report noted a longer than anticipated claims resolution process, but the loss and the expected cash outflows appear for the first time in the third-quarter report. Management's confidence that the claims will be recovered is management language, not evidence of recovery, and internal control over financial reporting was assessed effective at 2025-09-30.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2024-09-30_acm_acm-20240930x10k.htm.jsonl, page 82; 10-K_2025-09-30_acm_acm-20250930.htm.jsonl, pages 73–75; 10-K_2025-09-30_acm_acm-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 127; 10-Q_2026-01-02_acm_acm-20260102.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-Q_2026-04-03_acm_acm-20260403.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-Q_2026-04-03_acm_acm-20260403.htm.jsonl, page 53; 10-Q_2026-07-03_acm_acm-20260703.htm.jsonl, page 41; 10-Q_2026-07-03_acm_acm-20260703.htm.jsonl, page 55; calculation A06

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Acquisitions are small and are not the driver of the credit story, but goodwill makes book equity a thin cushion. Two acquisitions in fiscal 2025 cost $375.9 million in total, of which $146.4 million was paid in Aecom shares, and goodwill is 1.72x AECOM stockholders' equity.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_acm_acm-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 90; 10-Q_2026-07-03_acm_acm-20260703.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-07-03_acm_acm-20260703.htm.jsonl, page 12; calculation A09; calculation A12

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against caution is that the loss is concentrated and the rest of the business is improving: the International margin rose to 10.35% from 8.79%, remaining performance obligations were $20.4bn at 2026-06-30, and two legacy claims have been collected or settled, USD 51.1 million in the third quarter of fiscal 2026 and USD 58.5 million agreed in July 2026, which shows that large claims can be collected, although each followed a write-down of expected proceeds of USD 53.0 million and USD 61.8 million, so collection has been slower and lower than first expected. Claims recorded in contract assets of about $620 million are close to the low end of the expected outflows of USD 600 million to USD 800 million, so full and timely recovery would offset much of the cash cost, which is an analyst inference and not a management position.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-07-03_acm_acm-20260703.htm.jsonl, pages 10–11; 10-Q_2026-07-03_acm_acm-20260703.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-Q_2026-07-03_acm_acm-20260703.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-Q_2026-07-03_acm_acm-20260703.htm.jsonl, page 37; 10-Q_2026-07-03_acm_acm-20260703.htm.jsonl, page 55; calculation A03

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The view would improve if the claims are collected, if the fourth-quarter outflow stays within USD 175 million to USD 225 million, and if repurchases stay paused until then. It would weaken if either project needs a further loss estimate, if a client files a claim against Aecom, if the outflows exceed USD 800 million, or if repurchases resume while the claims remain uncollected.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Holder percentages, board independence, committee roles and executive pay are not established because the proxy statement is not supplied, so the conclusion that no controlling holder exists would change if a large holder were disclosed there.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The size of the Construction Management business, the identity of its clients and the contract terms of the two delayed projects are not stated, so the exposure conclusion rests on management's estimates, which the third-quarter report says may change and could be material.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The dates on which the strategic review of the Construction Management business began and ended are not stated, so the decision to keep the business cannot be placed against the project losses.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Backlog is printed only in the annual reports, so the order-book support for revenue rests on the figure at 2025-09-30 and any change since then is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The credit agreements and the indenture are summarised in the filings and not supplied, so the scope of the liens and guarantees, and how the guarantor group's weakness bears on each class of creditor, rests on those summaries.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: On 2026-03-10 Aecom replaced its revolver and term loans with a $1.5bn revolving credit facility and a $950 million term loan A, both maturing on 2031-03-10, and a $500 million term loan B maturing on 2031-04-19. Both term loans were borrowed in full and the proceeds repaid the previous facilities, which had a revolver and term loan A maturing in 2029 and a term loan B maturing in 2031. Bank debt outstanding was USD 1,448.8 million at 2026-06-30 against USD 1,439.9 million at 2025-09-30, so the amendment extended maturities without adding material debt.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: On 2026-06-10 a separate $500 million revolving facility maturing on 2028-06-09 was added under a new agreement, and it was undrawn with no letters of credit at 2026-06-30. Both bank agreements are secured by liens on substantially all assets of the company and the guarantors, and a consolidated leverage ratio of at most 4.00x is tested quarterly; the covenant does not apply to the term loan B and the company reported compliance at 2026-06-30.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: On 2025-07-22 Aecom issued $1.2bn of unsecured senior notes due 2033 and used the proceeds to retire the 2027 senior notes: most were bought in a July 2025 tender offer and the remainder was redeemed in August 2025, with make-whole payments of $9.1 million in total. The notes' estimated fair value at 2026-06-30 was $1,201.5 million, close to principal.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Acquisitions and disposals have been small or already completed. Two businesses were bought in fiscal 2025 for $375.9 million, including $146.4 million of Aecom shares; the Management Services and self-perform construction businesses were exited earlier and remain in discontinued operations; and the AECOM Capital team moved to a third-party platform in fiscal 2024. The strategic review of the Construction Management business, which the 2025 annual report said could include a sale, was later reported complete with a decision to keep and operate it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_acm_acm-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-K_2025-09-30_acm_acm-20250930.htm.jsonl, pages 7–8; 10-K_2025-09-30_acm_acm-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 90; 10-Q_2026-01-02_acm_acm-20260102.htm.jsonl, page 37; 10-Q_2026-04-03_acm_acm-20260403.htm.jsonl, page 40; 10-Q_2026-07-03_acm_acm-20260703.htm.jsonl, pages 9–10; calculation A12

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Shareholder returns are the main use of cash apart from debt service. The Board raised the repurchase authorization to $1.0bn on 2024-11-15 and approved an increase to $1.0bn again on 2026-02-04, with $884 million remaining at 2026-06-30, and the quarterly dividend was raised to USD 0.31 per share on 2025-11-18.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Three events dated after 2026-06-30 are outside the period figures: a quarterly dividend of USD 0.31 per share was paid on 2026-07-17, a settlement of the legacy Department of Energy claims will bring $58.5 million to Aecom with the receipt date not stated, and in August 2026 the tax authority sent a draft notice proposing adjustments to research credits claimed for fiscal 2017 through fiscal 2020, which Aecom disputes and could be material if sustained in full. No new debt or acquisition after 2026-06-30 is stated in the filings.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Sponsor / Governance Risk Level: Medium. The level is driven by the Construction Management exposure and returns exceeding operating cash flow, because they consume liquidity while claims remain uncollected, which implies a thinner creditor cushion. Countervailing evidence is the extended bank maturity profile, the paused repurchases and the diversified client base. Further analysis requires the proxy statement, the executed credit documents and project-level data.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Fundamental credit assessment of Aecom (acm-868857), as of 2026-11-18, on the credit snapshot pathway. The scope is the business, financial profile, outlook, downside path and monitoring triggers drawn from five filings through the quarter ended 2026-06-30 and the three supplied analyses.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Aecom's fundamental credit is adequate but weakening: two delayed projects and shareholder returns have raised leverage sharply, leaving creditors a thinner cushion through fiscal 2027 but no material refinancing pressure before 2031.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Net leverage was 2.31x at 2026-06-30 against 1.11x at 2025-09-30, or 2.36x pro forma for the dividend paid on 2026-07-17 and 2.24x if the USD 58.5 million settlement agreed in July 2026 is received in full, each taken alone. Cash plus undrawn revolvers covers the expected USD 600 million to USD 800 million of project outflows 3.45x at the top of the range, and scheduled maturities to fiscal 2030 are only USD 117.8 million. The main risks are claims left uncollected, outflows above the range and repurchases resuming.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-07-03_acm_acm-20260703.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-07-03_acm_acm-20260703.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-07-03_acm_acm-20260703.htm.jsonl, page 55; calculation B01; calculation B02; calculation B05; calculation B10

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The business profile is adequate to good for creditors, because scale, a government-funded client base and a large order book give revenue visibility that the third-quarter loss does not undermine. Governments supply 50% of revenue, no client reaches 10%, backlog was $39.7bn at 2025-09-30 and remaining performance obligations were $20.4bn at 2026-06-30, about 60% of them due within twelve months. The work is fee-based and asset-light, so a downturn in one market is cushioned by the others.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-09-30_acm_acm-20250930.htm.jsonl, pages 10–13; 10-Q_2026-07-03_acm_acm-20260703.htm.jsonl, page 15; calculation B18

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The financial profile has deteriorated in fiscal 2026 because earnings fell, not because Aecom borrowed more. Calculated EBITDA for the last twelve months is 29.63% below FY2025 while gross debt is almost unchanged, so total leverage rose to 3.21x from 2.26x, interest cover on accrued interest fell to 4.18x from 6.52x, and free cash flow fell to 0.24x of EBITDA from 0.57x. Cash interest cover for the latest period is not established because the quarterly reports print no cash interest.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation B01; calculation B03; calculation B04

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Two Construction Management projects are the single most important credit variable. One project took a loss of USD 336.8 million in the third quarter, management expects net cash outflows of USD 600 million to USD 800 million to finish two projects before any claim inflows, claims of about $620 million sit in contract assets, and Aecom has given the clients USD 403.9 million of letters of credit and USD 1.0 billion of surety bonds. Guaranteed-maximum-price and fixed-price work is 61.61% of revenue, so cost overruns land on Aecom, and the projects now account for more than the whole 12-day rise in days sales outstanding to 86 days.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-07-03_acm_acm-20260703.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-Q_2026-07-03_acm_acm-20260703.htm.jsonl, pages 35–36; 10-Q_2026-07-03_acm_acm-20260703.htm.jsonl, page 55; 10-Q_2026-07-03_acm_acm-20260703.htm.jsonl, page 56; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation B12; calculation B13; calculation B15

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Shareholder returns turned a manageable project outflow into a leverage problem, but the lever is in management's hands. Repurchases plus dividends were 3.29x operating cash flow in the nine months to 2026-06-30 and 8.04x free cash flow, against 0.38x operating cash flow a year earlier. Management says delayed claims could constrain repurchases, none were made from April to June 2026, and USD 884 million of authorization remains, so creditors depend on the pause lasting until the claims are collected.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-07-03_acm_acm-20260703.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-Q_2026-07-03_acm_acm-20260703.htm.jsonl, page 40; 10-Q_2026-07-03_acm_acm-20260703.htm.jsonl, page 41; 10-Q_2026-07-03_acm_acm-20260703.htm.jsonl, page 67; calculation B09; calculation B18

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity and the maturity profile are the main support against the downside. Cash excluding joint-venture cash plus undrawn revolvers covers the full expected outflow 3.45x to 4.60x, only 4.29% of principal falls due through fiscal 2030, the bank facilities now mature in 2031 or 2028 for the new USD 500 million revolver, and the 2033 senior notes were valued at 100.13% of principal at 2026-06-30. Management states that liquidity is sufficient for at least the next twelve months.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-07-03_acm_acm-20260703.htm.jsonl, pages 19–22; 10-Q_2026-07-03_acm_acm-20260703.htm.jsonl, page 54; calculation B05; calculation B10; calculation B16

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Structure and covenants are where the credit cannot be fully tested. A consolidated leverage ratio of at most 4.00x is tested quarterly, but its definition and the reported ratio are not printed, so headroom is not established; the bank lenders hold liens on substantially all assets while the 2033 notes are unsecured; and the parent and guarantor group lost USD 168.5 million in nine months and holds 55.66% of consolidated revenue. Goodwill is 1.72x stockholders' equity, so book equity is a thin cushion.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-07-03_acm_acm-20260703.htm.jsonl, pages 21–23; 10-Q_2026-07-03_acm_acm-20260703.htm.jsonl, pages 63–64; calculation B14; calculation B17

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The primary downside path is slow or partial claim recovery while outflows run to the top of the range. On reported EBITDA, paying USD 600 million to USD 800 million lifts net leverage to 3.02x to 3.25x before any claim inflow, an illustrative figure that holds everything else constant, against 2.16x to 2.33x if EBITDA were measured before the third-quarter loss. Which of the two is closer depends on whether the project loss is a one-off, which the filings do not settle.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-07-03_acm_acm-20260703.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-Q_2026-07-03_acm_acm-20260703.htm.jsonl, page 55; calculation B06; calculation B07

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against a weakening view is that the damage is concentrated and may prove temporary. Before the USD 336.8 million loss, last-twelve-months EBITDA would have been close to the FY2025 level, so net leverage on that basis would be 1.65x, well below the reported figure; the International segment margin rose to 10.35% from 8.79%; two legacy claims have already been collected or settled; repurchases are paused; and claims of about $620 million are 1.03x the low end of the expected outflows, so full recovery would roughly offset the cash cost, an analyst inference and not a management position.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-07-03_acm_acm-20260703.htm.jsonl, pages 10–11; 10-Q_2026-07-03_acm_acm-20260703.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-Q_2026-07-03_acm_acm-20260703.htm.jsonl, page 37; 10-Q_2026-07-03_acm_acm-20260703.htm.jsonl, page 55; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation B07; calculation B08; calculation B11

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The view would improve if claims are collected, if the fourth-quarter outflow stays within USD 175 million to USD 225 million, if repurchases stay paused until then, and if the fiscal 2026 annual report shows covenant room. It would weaken if either project needs a further loss estimate, if a client files a claim, if outflows exceed USD 800 million, if repurchases resume while claims are uncollected, or if the tax authority's draft proposal on research credits proves large.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The covenant ratio, its definition and its headroom are not printed, so the conclusion that leverage is manageable rests on the 4.00x limit stated and on leverage built from the statements, and true headroom could be narrower than the house measures suggest.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The downside arithmetic holds EBITDA and every other cash flow constant and ignores claim inflows, so it sizes the project cash effect and is not a forecast of leverage at fiscal year-end.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No filing after the quarter ended 2026-06-30 is supplied, so the fourth-quarter outflow, any new loss estimate and the fiscal 2026 year-end balance sheet are not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No ratings, peer set or market pricing other than the fair value of the 2033 notes is supplied, so market access and the comparison with typical leveraged issuers are not established and the assessment rests on maturities, liquidity and the issuer's own history.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Cash interest paid for the last twelve months is not printed, so interest cover is shown on accrued expense and the conclusion that debt service is comfortable rests on a proxy.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Scale and a diversified public-sector client base are the first credit strength. Governments supply 50% of revenue, no client reaches 10%, and backlog of $39.7bn at 2025-09-30 gives revenue visibility, so the business can absorb a problem in one project or market without losing its cash-generating base, which lowers the chance that a single event threatens debt service.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-09-30_acm_acm-20250930.htm.jsonl, pages 10–13; calculation B18

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity and the maturity profile are the second strength. Cash excluding joint-venture cash plus undrawn revolvers covers the full expected project outflow 3.45x to 4.60x and only 4.29% of principal falls due through fiscal 2030, so the project cash cost can be paid without a refinancing, and the bank maturity extension to 2031 removes the nearest pressure point.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-07-03_acm_acm-20260703.htm.jsonl, pages 19–22; calculation B05; calculation B10

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: A flexible financial policy with no sponsor is the third strength. No sponsor extracts cash, repurchases were paused from April to June 2026, and management has tied their timing to claim collection, so net leverage can rebuild if the pause lasts, although the stated link is not a commitment.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Price risk on construction work is the first weakness. Guaranteed-maximum-price and fixed-price contracts are 61.61% of revenue, and on two Construction Management projects delays raised the cost to complete, producing a loss of USD 336.8 million and expected net cash outflows of USD 600 million to USD 800 million, which lifts net debt by the amount paid and exposes Aecom to further estimate changes and to client claims.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_acm_acm-20250930.htm.jsonl, pages 11–12; 10-Q_2026-07-03_acm_acm-20260703.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-Q_2026-07-03_acm_acm-20260703.htm.jsonl, page 55; calculation B12

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weak cash conversion is the second weakness. Free cash flow was 0.24x of EBITDA over the last twelve months against 0.57x in FY2025 because claims and receivables absorbed cash, and days sales outstanding rose to 86 days, so less cash is available to cut debt or to cover interest even before the project outflows.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-07-03_acm_acm-20260703.htm.jsonl, page 56; calculation B04; calculation B13

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Returns that exceeded operating cash flow are the third weakness. Repurchases plus dividends were 3.29x operating cash flow in nine months, so cash fell while debt did not, and the cushion built in FY2025 was spent on shareholders instead of on leverage.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Untested structure and covenants are the fourth weakness. The covenant ratio is not printed, the parent and guarantor group lost USD 168.5 million in nine months, and goodwill is 1.72x stockholders' equity, so creditors cannot confirm headroom or rely on book equity if earnings fall further.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-07-03_acm_acm-20260703.htm.jsonl, page 21; 10-Q_2026-07-03_acm_acm-20260703.htm.jsonl, pages 63–64; calculation B14; calculation B17

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Aecom supplies planning, design, engineering, program management and construction management services to governments and private clients in transportation, facilities, water, environment and energy, and earns its income mainly by billing employee time, so cash generation depends on utilisation and collections and not on capital spent. Americas supplies most of revenue (22.39% comes from International) and AECOM Capital is a real estate investment segment with negligible revenue but continuing guarantees. The model supports debt service because most costs flex with staff and subcontractors, but it weakens liquidity when projects carry price risk, as the two Construction Management projects show.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-09-30_acm_acm-20250930.htm.jsonl, pages 4–5; calculation B21

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Ownership is widely dispersed with no sponsor, parent or controlling holder disclosed, so financial policy is set by the board and management, and creditor protection rests on covenants and on the company's own cash flow, not on sponsor support. The guarantors are wholly owned subsidiaries; the bank lenders hold liens on substantially all assets of the company and the guarantors, the 2033 notes are unsecured, and the parent and guarantor group is smaller and weaker than the consolidated company. Holder percentages, board independence and related-party dealings are not established because the proxy statement is not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue is predictable and largely public-sector funded, but its quality is lower than headline revenue suggests. Pass-through subcontractor cost was 53% of fiscal 2025 revenue, work is awarded project by project, and government clients can terminate or renegotiate contracts at their convenience with many contracts renewed annually. Backlog of $39.7bn is gross of pass-through costs and $20.0bn above the obligations the accounting standard counts, so the credit consequence is good visibility but limited pricing power, because the markets are fragmented and entry barriers are low.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-09-30_acm_acm-20250930.htm.jsonl, pages 13–16; 10-K_2025-09-30_acm_acm-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 53; calculation B18

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Margins can be defended against volume pressure but not against project overruns. Costs flex with staff and subcontractors, yet the nine-month Americas margin fell to 3.66% from 6.79% on one project while International rose to 10.35% from 8.79%, so margin stability depends on execution risk and not on demand. Restructuring spend of about USD 25 million is expected in fiscal 2026 and is meant to support margin improvement.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-07-03_acm_acm-20260703.htm.jsonl, page 37; 10-Q_2026-07-03_acm_acm-20260703.htm.jsonl, pages 54–55; calculation B11; calculation B19

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash conversion is the weakest part of the profile. Capital expenditure is only 1.05% of last-twelve-months revenue, so capex is not the problem, but free cash flow fell to 0.24x of EBITDA from 0.57x because claims and receivables absorbed cash, and the two projects explain the whole rise in days sales outstanding to 86 days. EBITDA turns into durable free cash flow for debt service only if the claims are collected.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-07-03_acm_acm-20260703.htm.jsonl, page 56; calculation B04; calculation B13; calculation B20

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Rivalry is high and barriers to entry are low. The filing describes highly fragmented markets with many competitors, some larger or more specialised, and services that need little upfront capital, so Aecom competes on reputation, cost, client relationships and its network. Buyer power is strong because governments supply 50% of revenue and can terminate or renegotiate contracts at their convenience, although no single client reaches 10%. Supplier power matters through subcontractors, whose cost is passed through on cost-reimbursable work but not on fixed-price or guaranteed-maximum-price work, and technology change is addressed through investment in digital and AI tools. These forces cap margins and mean credit quality relies on scale, contract discipline and client relationships.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-09-30_acm_acm-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-K_2025-09-30_acm_acm-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-K_2025-09-30_acm_acm-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-K_2025-09-30_acm_acm-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 16; calculation B18

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Policy and funding are material to credit because half of revenue is public. Funded programs such as the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act and the One Big Beautiful Bill Act in the United States, federal programs in Canada and the ten-year infrastructure strategy in the United Kingdom support demand, while government shutdowns, changes in administration and funding directives, and trade policy are named risks, and International is 22.39% of revenue and exposed to currency moves. A funding delay would slow billings and add to working capital, which is the channel through which policy risk reaches debt service.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_acm_acm-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 44; 10-Q_2026-07-03_acm_acm-20260703.htm.jsonl, page 39; 10-Q_2026-07-03_acm_acm-20260703.htm.jsonl, page 44; calculation B21

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: In credit terms the strengths are scale and diversification across clients and regions, a fee-based and asset-light model, liquidity and maturities, and a repurchase lever. The weaknesses are fixed-price project risk, weak cash conversion, a thin guarantor group equity base and unprinted covenant headroom. The factors that could improve credit quality are collection of claims, continued growth in backlog and a sustained International margin, and the factors that could weaken it are further loss estimates, client claims, a large tax adjustment and resumed repurchases.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-07-03_acm_acm-20260703.htm.jsonl, page 29; 10-Q_2026-07-03_acm_acm-20260703.htm.jsonl, page 41

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: On a ratings-style reading the profile is mixed and the trend is down. Scale and market position are strong, with fiscal 2025 revenue of $16.1bn and a self-described leading position in design that is management language citing a trade survey, while competitive advantage is average because entry barriers are low. Business diversification is strong across clients and regions but weaker across contract types, cost and capex flexibility is strong on capex and average on costs, and margin stability and free cash flow stability are weak this year, with free cash flow at 0.24x of EBITDA.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-09-30_acm_acm-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-K_2025-09-30_acm_acm-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-K_2025-09-30_acm_acm-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 74; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation B04; calculation B18

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Access to capital markets and liquidity are the stronger side of the profile: maturities are long, the 2033 notes were valued at 100.13% of principal and cash plus undrawn revolvers covers the expected outflows 3.45x to 4.60x. Financial policy and governance are average to weak: returns exceeded cash flow, the chair and chief executive roles are combined, and the claims disclosure came late, but no sponsor extracts cash and repurchases are paused. The main supports are scale, liquidity and maturities, the main constraints are project risk and cash conversion, and the key missing datapoints are the covenant ratio, project-level data and the fourth-quarter result.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-07-03_acm_acm-20260703.htm.jsonl, page 22; calculation B05; calculation B09; calculation B16

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over the next 12 to 24 months the credit depends on how the two projects finish. The expected outflow is USD 175 million to USD 225 million in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026 and the rest in fiscal 2027, restructuring costs of about USD 25 million remain, and management states that liquidity is sufficient for at least the next twelve months, so the period is a test of cash discipline: leverage will stay above the pre-loss level until claims are collected or earnings recover.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over three to five years the maturity wall sits beyond the horizon: 95.71% of principal falls after fiscal 2030, mainly the 2031 bank facilities and the 2033 notes, which are callable from 2028-08-01 at a premium. Refinancing then depends on leverage returning toward prior levels and on the business holding its public-sector funding, so the medium-term question is whether net leverage rebuilds from its reported level rather than whether markets are open.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-07-03_acm_acm-20260703.htm.jsonl, pages 19–23; calculation B01; calculation B10

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Sector tailwinds are funded infrastructure programs, national defence spending, energy and data centre demand and water investment, which management cites as supporting revenue, with defence spending also raising backlog and pipeline. Sector headwinds are funding delays, shutdowns and trade policy. Company tailwinds are the International margin and restructuring savings, and company headwinds are claims timing, a larger working capital base, a draft tax adjustment on research credits that could be material if sustained in full, and an interest burden that rose after the 2025 notes issue.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_acm_acm-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 44; 10-Q_2026-07-03_acm_acm-20260703.htm.jsonl, page 29; 10-Q_2026-07-03_acm_acm-20260703.htm.jsonl, page 44; 10-Q_2026-07-03_acm_acm-20260703.htm.jsonl, page 46; 10-Q_2026-07-03_acm_acm-20260703.htm.jsonl, pages 54–55; calculation B04; calculation B11

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The initiating condition is that claims resolution keeps slipping while the two Construction Management projects need the full expected cash. The first operational break is that the completion cost lands in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026 and fiscal 2027 while working capital stays inflated at 86 days, so operating cash flow remains weak. The financial transmission is that net debt rises by the amount paid: on reported EBITDA, paying USD 600 million to USD 800 million lifts net leverage from its reported level to 3.02x to 3.25x, an illustrative figure with everything else held constant.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-07-03_acm_acm-20260703.htm.jsonl, page 55; 10-Q_2026-07-03_acm_acm-20260703.htm.jsonl, page 56; calculation B01; calculation B06; calculation B13

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The liquidity consequence is limited, because cash plus undrawn revolvers covers the full outflow 3.45x to 4.60x and only USD 117.8 million of debt falls due through fiscal 2030, so no refinancing is forced. The leverage consequence is where stress would show first: total leverage of 3.21x is nearer than net leverage to the 4.00x covenant limit, whose definition is not printed, so headroom is not established. Management levers are the paused repurchases, the dividend, restructuring and working capital, and resilience appears sufficient to avoid liquidity distress unless client claims or a large tax adjustment arrive at the same time. The observable triggers are a further loss estimate, a client claim, outflows above USD 800 million and repurchases resuming.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-07-03_acm_acm-20260703.htm.jsonl, page 21; 10-Q_2026-07-03_acm_acm-20260703.htm.jsonl, pages 35–36; 10-Q_2026-07-03_acm_acm-20260703.htm.jsonl, page 41; calculation B02; calculation B05; calculation B10

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, Aecom presents an adequate business profile supported by scale, client diversification and a large order book, but credit quality is constrained by fixed-price project exposure, weak cash conversion and shareholder returns that exceeded cash flow. Cash-flow durability appears adequate in a normal year and weak this year, because free cash flow fell to 0.24x of EBITDA while the projects absorb cash. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on claims being collected, repurchases staying paused and leverage returning toward 1.11x, and maturities are not pressing. The primary downside path is slow or partial claim recovery while outflows reach the top of the range. The comparison with typical leveraged-credit issuers in the sector is not established because no peer set is supplied. Further analysis would require the covenant ratio and definition, project-level data, the fiscal 2026 annual report and the proxy statement. The top risk is the cash cost and contingent exposure of the two Construction Management projects.
